3059: 200 years old immortal alchemy teacher wanting to know what he could not know. Doing anything in his will to get it. A seemingly geriatric alchemist who gains immortality during the 1711 incident aboard the Advena Avis.
3060: Szilard's homunculus, though not his first creation. She was created to unthinkingly execute his every command; recently, however, she has been gaining emotions as well as independent thought, as a result of 'devouring' an alchemist threatening Szilard's life.
3061: The youngest executive of Manhattan's Martillo Family Camorra. Firo is surprisingly friendly, humorous and compassionate, but he is a skilled fighter and can be ruthless or even vengeful towards those who bring harm to the people he cares about.
3062: Ladd's lover and fiancée. She is fair-haired and beautiful, despite sporting a somewhat vacant (albeit serene) expression. She is completely devoted to Ladd and is likely a masochist, as she seems to take pleasure in his promise that he will be the one to kill her.
3063: The youngest Advenna Avis immortal. His guardian, Ferment, tortured him to test the limits of immortality. Czeslaw manages to devour Ferment, ending his suffering. Unfortunately, he learns from Fermet's memories that he was simply being tortured for Femet's own self-satisfaction.
3064: Eve is the little sister of Dallas Genoard. Despite her quiet personality and aristocratic upbringing, Eve has very little fear of the New York streets, going directly against the mafia as she searches for her brother. Eve truly believes that Dallas has a kind heart.
3065: Ladd is a sadistic hit-man for the Russo family. His love for acts of violence truly shows in the maniacal glee he exhibits while fighting or killing. He is exceptionally skilled in hand-to-hand combat—particularly boxing—and the use of firearms.
3498: Bookkeeper of the Martillo family and one of the Advena Avis immortals. His younger brother, Gretto, was one of the first to be "devoured" for knowledge of the elixir's recipe.
3499: Nice Holystone is a bomb enthusiast and the girlfriend of Jacuzzi Splot. She co-leads Jacuzzi's Gang. Nice's skin is marred by scars (on the right side of her face and across her arms) thanks to an accident in her youth.
3500: A crybaby who is nonetheless capable of exceptional courage and leadership ability when the situation calls for it. At first, Jacuzzi seems almost cripplingly shy, even with a tendency to stutter in front of strangers.
3637: Carol is the assistant to the vice president of The Daily Days; Gustav Saint Germain. She is inquisitive and is constantly awarded meaningless points for every answer she gives to the vice president, making her inquire "Out of how many?".
3662: Issac Dian forms one half of the bumbling thief couple, who seem to cross into everybody's story in one way or another. He's in love with Miria, and they've robbed everything and anything, from doors to the entire Genoard household.
3754: A young man always seen smiling with a pair of scissors. The son of a clockmaker, as a child he was sold by his stepfather to a young Luck Gandor as a means of payment for an $2500 loan his stepfather couldn't pay off.
3796: Another eccentric thief, she is the partner and lover of Isaac Dian. Miria wholeheartedly believes and supports everything Isaac says, often even going so far as to mimic his body language.
3873: Intelligent executive of the Mafia Gandor Family. The third of the brothers and childhood friend of Firo, having grown up in the same apartment block. Although he and his brothers lead the Gandor family, Luck's close ties with Firo makes the Gandors allies of the Martillo Family.
4169: The vice president of the Daily Days. He works with his assistant Carol primarily on incidents involving immortals. St. Germain is a pseudonym he borrows from the famous alchemist the Count of St. Germain.
5756: The youngest train conductor for the Flying Pussy Foot, he tells Miria and Isaac the story of the dreaded "Rail-Tracer", a story about a brutish beast that causes passengers in a train to disappear one by one.
7092: The beautiful, dagger wielding daughter of Huey Laforet. Although her father is one of the original immortals who had been aboard the Advena Avis in 1711, she is actually mortal.
7093: She was initially hired as an assassin by the Runorata family, but was opposed to them and eventually pledged her loyalty to the Gandor Family. Despite her womanly looks, she's still very childish in nature.
8132: An information broker for the Daily Days, its Chief Editor, and the copy editor of the newspaper's English edition. Much of Nicholas' personality in the anime is actually Henry's.
8861: One of Advena Avis immortals. Aside from Elmer, Huey sees everyone, including his own children, as possible test subjects for his experiments. Huey has many groups, of both humans and non-humans (his homunculi), working under him, like the Lemures and the Lamia.
10523: Maiza Avaro's younger brother, Sylvie Lumiere's boyfriend, and a passenger aboard the Advena Avis.
11903: One of the Advena Avis immortals. Elmer was born into a religious cult where the sole purpose of his existence was to be an object of abuse. He later moved to Lotto Valentino where he went to the same alchemy school as Huey and Monica.
12538: A freelancer for the Daily Days information center. As the daughter of a train engineer, who was driven to ruin after being unjustly blamed for a horrific train accident, Rachel loves trains but is bitter towards the train industry.
12948: An Advena Avis immortal and only woman aboard the ship. She saved her share of the immortality elixir and drank it a few years after the rest of the passengers. After her lover, Gretto, was devoured by Szilard, she decided to devote her life to seeking revenge for his death.
13081: Eve Genoard's older brother and a troublemaker. He comes from the wealthy Genoard family that has close ties with the Runorata Mafia Family.
26694: Dune was part of the original group of men that Ladd Russo assembled for the kidnapping aboard the 'Flying Pussyfoot'. To get aboard he killed the about-to-retire conductor 'Tony' and stole his conductor uniform and subsequently wore it.
29626: Keith is the oldest of the Gandor brothers (being somewhere in his late twenties or early thirties) and with his two younger brothers Berga and Luck inherited the Gandor mafia family from their father.
29627: Berga is the second oldest Gandor son and with his two brothers runs the Gandor family mafia. Of the three brothers he seems to enjoy violence the most (this is excluding Claire, their "4th" brother), and seems to do most of the mafia's dirty work alongside Mr.
30199: The aging conductor of the Flying Pussyfoot who "passes the torch" to his protege, Claire Stanfield, shortly before the voyage during which much of the story unfolds.
30200: The young daughter of Senator Manfred Beriam, she and her mother Natalie are held as political hostages aboard the Flying Pussyfoot.
31290: One of the Lamia homunculi created by Huey. Her main weapon is a cross-shaped spear.
32013: A senator whose wife and daughter are held as hostages aboard the Flying Pussyfoot. Doing this, the terrorists are trying to get his support in freeing Huey Laforet.
36130: The wife of Senator Manfred Beriam, and the mother of Mary Beriam. She and her daughter are held as hostages while aboard "The Flying Pussyfoot".
38427: The president is the unseen head of the Daily Days. His office is filled with paper and the sound of ringing phones. His age is unknown due to the large mountain of papers on his desk, but he is described as having a young voice.
39148: Fermet was one of the original immortals from 1711. He was guardian to the orphaned Czeslaw Meyer.
41204: Ladd's uncle, and the don of the Russo family. Placido is very brash and will not tolerate any error from his thugs, though he seems to genuinely care for his grandchild Ricardo. After Ladd leaves the family, he begins to lose the power he once had.
43177: The head of Huey's group who are on the Flying Pussyfoot.
43508: A member of Jacuzzi's Gang. At the end of December 1931, he is one of the gang members who participates in a robbery of the Flying Pussyfoot transcontinental express, and one of the men who holds up its dining car. During the heist, he is captured twice by the Lemures.
43602: She works for the Martillo Family as a waitress at Alveare. She is the older sister of Fang Lin-Shan.
60393: One of the Advena Avis immortals. On the Advenna Avis, he saves Sylvie from Szilard. After becoming immortal, he begins to visit various battlefields in order to not forget the meaning of death but ends up desensitized to it instead.
64567: A calm, expressionless man who moves between organizations and jobs as it suits him. He has a good grasp of his abilities and his competency.
68433: An Englishman who arrived in Lotto Valentino in the 1700s alongside fellow Dormentaire-sponsored alchemist Szilard Quates in order to investigate the city's illicit activities.
72357: An Advenna Avis immortal. After landing in America in 1711 he attempts to walk back to Japan but ends up buried in ice somewhere around the North Pole. He is eventually found by a Soviet nuclear submarine and ends up going on the run from the KGB for most of the Cold War.
72853: One of the 1711 immortals. He studied together under the same alchemy teacher as Fermet. In the 1930's Begg works for the Runorata Family. Begg spends his time trying to create the perfect drug to bring people "happiness."
77611: He works as a bartender on the Flying Pussyfoot in 1931, and together with Fang Lin-Shan.
284421: A delinquent member of Jacuzzi's Gang with a leisurely, laid-back countenance. In December 1931, she is part of the retrieval team tasked with retrieving the stolen cargo from the Flying Pussyfoot as it is dumped into a river.

329997: A federal agent who primarily handles incidents involving immortals.
329998: A federal agent from the Federal Bureau of Investigation who deals with incidents involving immortals. He strongly dislikes Maiza Avaro and Firo Prochainezo and has a strong sense of justice.
329999: A federal employee who handles cases involving immortals.

330006: An Italian immigrant, and the don of the Martillo Family.
330007: A Japanese immigrant and the elderly primo voto of the Martillo Family.
330008: An executive of the Martillo Family.
330009: An executive of the Martillo Family.
330011: One of the White Suits who hijacked the transcontinental express Flying Pussyfoot on December 30, 1931.

330013: The longstanding butler of the Genoard Family, and one of the only two employees to remain with Eve Genoard following the loss of the Genoard heads and factories in December 1931.
330015: A longstanding maid of the Genoard Family, and one of the only two employees to remain with Eve Genoard following the loss of the Genoard heads and factories in December 1931.
330017: An information broker at the Daily Days and the copy editor of the newspaper's Chinese edition. He plays a role in aiding Eve Genoard's search for her brother Dallas Genoard.
330018: The incomplete immortal responsible for overseeing and managing the blenders (chemists) who work on Szilard Quates' infamous Cure-All Elixir.
330021: The proprietress of the Alveare, a specialty honey shop and speakeasy-turned-restaurant under Martillo Family control.
330023: A member of Jacuzzi's Gang who participates in the retrieval side of the Flying Pussyfoot robbery in 1931. Despite opposition from Sarges and the Lemures, she and the rest of the retrieval team are successful in recovering the train's cargo.
